extracted.intended_audience: NLP / NLG researchers and practitioners building or evaluating automatic story evaluators and reward models for story generation
extracted.subtask_description: Designing, training, and validating automatic evaluators for open-ended story generation, including creation and selection of chain-of-thought rationales, pairwise evaluation frameworks, and use as reward models for RL-based story generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the HANNA evaluation dimensions (and considered in OpenMEVA aspects): how relevant the story is to the prompt or intended topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a 1-to-5 Likert rating in HANNA; pairwise comparison increases inter-annotator agreement for Relevance (+0.063 difference, +12.5% improvement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence
rubrics_metrics.description: A core evaluation dimension (present in StoryER, HANNA, and OpenMEVA): the logical flow and connectedness of events, sentences, and narrative structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured on a 1-to-5 Likert scale in datasets; pairwise annotation substantially improves agreement on Coherence (+0.106, +21.9%). Emphasized as a critical aspect for human-aligned evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empathy
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation dimension indicating the story's ability to evoke or portray characters' feelings and emotional resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in StoryER and HANNA as a rated dimension on a 1–5 Likert scale; more subjective than Relevance/Coherence and tends to have lower inter-annotator agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: A dimension (HANNA) capturing novelty, unexpectedness, or plot twists that surprise the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured on a 1–5 scale; identified as more subjective with lower micro-level annotator agreement compared to objective criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement (Interestingness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures how engaging or interesting a story is to readers (referred to as 'Interestingness' in HANNA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as a separate HANNA dimension; treated as multi-aspect rating in pointwise and pairwise setups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: A HANNA dimension reflecting narrative or conceptual complexity of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among six HANNA dimensions; in the inter-annotator agreement study Complexity showed a marginal exception where pairwise did not improve agreement (-0.012).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: A StoryER dimension: quality and effectiveness of the story's ending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rated on the StoryER-Scale 1–5 Likert ratings; used as a fine-grained dimension for training and benchmarking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Style
rubrics_metrics.description: A StoryER dimension: the narrative voice, diction, and stylistic qualities of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of StoryER-Scale multi-aspect ratings; value for both training and evaluation though not directly used for EvolvR rationale supervision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development
rubrics_metrics.description: A StoryER dimension measuring depth and evolution of characters throughout the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided as fine-grained pointwise ratings in StoryER-Scale and used as a benchmark dimension for evaluating evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Quality (Holistic)
rubrics_metrics.description: The single holistic score provided by OpenMEVA representing overall story quality, aggregating aspects like relevance, fluency, coherence, and commonsense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OpenMEVA provides a 1–5 Likert overall quality score (no detailed breakdown). EvolvR averages its multi-dimension predictions to produce a single holistic score for zero-shot tests on OpenMEVA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluency
rubrics_metrics.description: Aspect considered by OpenMEVA: surface-level linguistic quality and readability (grammar, phrasing, naturalness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often subsumed into holistic scores; may be considered explicitly when comparing or designing reference-based evaluators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commonsense
rubrics_metrics.description: An OpenMEVA-considered aspect: commonsense plausibility and factual/logical world-knowledge consistency of events and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often evaluated implicitly within holistic ratings; important to ensure narratives do not contain blatant commonsense violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference-based / Pairwise Comparison Criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Use preference judgments (e.g., 'Story A is more creative than Story B') rather than absolute scores as the primary evaluation format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: comparative judgment aligns better with human cognitive processes and yields higher inter-annotator agreement across most dimensions. Empirical support: higher pairwise agreement for 5 of 6 HANNA dimensions and concrete % improvements (e.g., Coherence +21.9%, Relevance +12.5%). Also naturally compatible with RLHF paradigms and reward modeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Score-Aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT) Rationales
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate CoT rationales that are explicitly aligned to given ground-truth scores (CoT explains and justifies the assigned score).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EvolvR synthesizes score-aligned CoTs via multi-persona prompting (inputs: story, dimension, final score). CoTs must justify the score logically; later vetted by Self-Rule and human calibration. These rationales serve both as training targets and interpretability evidence for the evaluator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-Persona CoT Synthesis / Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Create a diverse corpus of CoT rationales by prompting models with multiple persona roles (Academic, Artist, Pragmatist, Sharp-Tongued Reader, Casual Netizen) to elicit varied reasoning styles and evaluation focuses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use few-shot prompts and multiple high-capability LLMs to maximize diversity; include human calibration by domain experts (e.g., professional screenwriters) to ensure logical soundness and score alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratified Sampling of Score Pairs
rubrics_metrics.description: When synthesizing pairwise data, perform stratified sampling to ensure balanced representation of all score-pair combinations (e.g., (1,2), (3,5), (4,4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents overfitting to natural distribution of score pairs and yields more robust training data covering the full range of comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position-Swapping to Mitigate Positional Bias
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment pairwise data by swapping the order of each story pair (create (A,B) and (B,A)) to force the model to base judgements on content rather than position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigates positional bias during both synthesis and evaluation. EvolvR evaluation protocol also performs swapped evaluations for robustness and stable aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CoT Evolution and Selection Pipeline (Rule → Refinement → Rule → Counter → Confidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: A staged multi-agent pipeline to filter and refine synthesized CoTs, applying repeated rule checks, refinement, adversarial counter-testing, and confidence scoring to ensure data quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence enforces score alignment at multiple stages, improves logical flow, removes weak or generic rationales (via counter checks), and selects only CoTs that decisively lead to correct scores. Documented survival rates show attrition from 800k initial to ~536k final CoTs (~67% survival), indicating stringency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Rule Agent: Exact Score Alignment Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent that enforces strict alignment between the CoT’s conclusion and the ground-truth scores; discards instances where parsed scores do not exactly match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements alignment checks (e.g., via regular expressions) and acts as a critical integrity filter after synthesis and after any modification step to ensure conclusions match ground-truth labels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Refinement Agent: Improve Logical Flow and Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Agent prompts the model to review and rewrite its own rationale to enhance logical flow, clarity, and persuasiveness without changing the underlying judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any CoT modified in this stage must pass a subsequent Self-Rule check to ensure it remains score-aligned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Counter Agent: Adversarial Robustness Testing
rubrics_metrics.description: Adversarially tests a CoT by inverting the final scores (e.g., flip preference) and prompting the model to detect contradictions between original reasoning and the inverted conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the model fails to detect contradictions implying the reasoning can support conflicting outcomes, the CoT is discarded. This filters out weak/generic rationales that lack discriminative power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-Confidence Agent: Decisive Confidence Selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Select CoTs that lead the model to the correct conclusion with highest confidence (the ground-truth score must have maximum softmax probability over score tokens when the CoT is concatenated with instruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute P(y=y*|Input, CoT) by extracting logits L(j) for score tokens and applying softmax; retain CoTs only if the ground-truth score is the argmax, ensuring rationales are not merely plausible but decisively lead to the correct judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensembling & Stability Testing Protocol (2N evaluations aggregate)
rubrics_metrics.description: For stable scoring, aggregate multiple pairwise evaluations: sample N other stories, form N pairs, evaluate each pair in both orders (yielding 2N scores), and aggregate to a single score for the target.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary N (1,2,4,8,16) to test robustness; reported metrics (Table 10) show how number of pairs affects Pearson/Spearman/Kendall correlations and MSE/F1. Swapping orders mitigates positional bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward Function Design for Pairwise GRPO
rubrics_metrics.description: Design reward for GRPO as an exponential function of cumulative absolute error: R(ya,yb) = exp(-λ(|ya−y* a| + |yb−y* b|)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a smooth signal maximized at 1 for perfect predictions and decays as error increases. Note: such reward can be exploited by degenerately predicting most frequent scores; monitor and mitigate degenerate policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composite Reward Signal for Generation
rubrics_metrics.description: When using EvolvR as a reward model for generation, combine multiple components: absolute predicted score, relative advantage, and a length reward penalty/bonus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice of reference story (static human exemplar vs dynamic base model generation) impacts training: pairing with base-model outputs produced better improvements in experiments, hypothesized to be due to more focused comparisons on stylistic/structural similarities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Objective for CoT Models
rubrics_metrics.description: Train Pointwise and Pairwise CoT models via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using a standard cross-entropy loss to predict CoT rationales and final scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use synthesized, vetted CoTs as training targets; monitor training loss curves (Figure 3) and validate via downstream correlation metrics against human judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Metrics and Reporting Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Use correlation and error metrics to measure evaluator performance: Pearson, Spearman, Kendall correlations; Mean Squared Error (MSE); F1-score; win rates in human evals; Average Score ± Standard Deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report higher-is-better for correlations and scores, lower-is-better for MSE and standard deviation (stability). Provide confusion matrices and per-score agreement analyses (Figure 5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inter-Expert Reliability (IRR) Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess human evaluation consistency by computing inter-expert correlations (e.g., Pearson r) at macro (average scores per model) and micro (individual stories per dimension) levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use benchmarks (e.g., HANNA ratings) as reference anchors for human annotators. High macro-level agreement (pairwise correlations > 0.91 reported) strengthens confidence in human ranking; micro-level correlations vary by dimension and reveal subjectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Positional Bias Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly analyze and report positional bias by comparing evaluator performance when input pairs are in (A,B) vs (B,A) order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report metrics for both positions (Table 11); incorporate swapping in data augmentation and evaluation to mitigate bias. EvolvR shows small differences between (A,B) and (B,A) when swaps are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-based Handling for Reference-required Metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For models that require a reference text (e.g., InstructScore, TIGERScore), use the story itself as its own reference when evaluating open-ended story generation to enable reference-free-style evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This self-reference approach permits zero-shot usage of models designed for reference-based inputs while keeping the evaluation comparable.
